topics.topic: Authoritative module for the fact-to-disclosure-class mapping
questions: Which module is the authoritative owner of fact disclosure classes, and is `PERSONAL_DATA_FIELDS` derived from that authority or independently authoritative?
Which module owns the fact-to-disclosure-class mapping used to classify answers?

quotes: The models M01–M12 as the domain's vocabulary, the declared vocabularies of State 1 as enumerations — for the artifact types only the shape of a type with its owner service, whose rows are `data_provider`'s, so a stored pointer of a type a later release removed still reads (A22 rule 4) — and the disclosure class of every fact ("Disclosure classes by field"), the order of the classes (A09 rule 4), and the refusal vocabulary: each refusal kind with the stage of A04 rule 6 it belongs to.

Which facts are `personal_data` ("Disclosure classes by field") is one table of the release, `data_provider`'s `PERSONAL_DATA_FIELDS`, of (answer model, field) pairs (owner, 2026-11-17); every other fact is `business_confidential` and none is `open`. `operations` computes an answer's class as the highest of its facts' — `personal_data` when one of those fields holds a value — and refuses the answer whole when it is above the caller's highest (A09 rule 4): a service's from `service_access`, and for the owner `personal_data`, the highest class, so no owner answer is refused for its class (Actors and trust boundaries, "Personal data").
judgement.why: `models` owns the domain classification of facts, while `data_provider` owns the release table through which `operations` applies that classification to answers.

topics.topic: Validation and handling of declared-length, transport-length, and multipart-ending failures
questions: What is the result when the request's declared length is smaller than the parsed head plus the required closing delimiter, does not match the bytes delivered by the transport, or the closing delimiter is missing or malformed?
Which multipart endings are accepted, which module refuses an invalid ending, and does such a refusal preserve the session's previously kept upload?

quotes: The multipart framing of an upload (owner, 2026-11-17): an upload form sends its CSRF field as the first part of its body and the file as the second, so that the CSRF value travels in a form (A13 rules 5, 7) and the file still reaches `migration_import` unread. Reading the body's head alone — the boundary the request's content type names, the first part, which must be the CSRF field, and the second part's headers — at most the data provider's `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES`, answering the CSRF value, or none for a head of another form or longer than the bound; and the file part's bytes as a stream that ends where the part ends, read only when its reader asks and never buffered beyond the delimiter it must look ahead for; and the file part's declared length — the request's declared length less the head it read and the closing delimiter with its final `--` and line end, or none when the request declares none — so that a file of exactly the import limit is not refused for its framing (A19 rule 4).

`capability:migration_import.read_import_mapping` refuses when the closure exists (rule 8), refuses a file over the imported `IMPORT_FILE_MAX_BYTES` constant (A19 rule 4) — reading the upload's stream, which `module:owner_interface` hands on unread with its declared length: a declared length over it refused before any byte is read, otherwise refused as soon as more than it has been read — and a file that cannot be read, holds two projects with one id, or a project without a readable id or status (rule 3), and otherwise answers each project with its id and status. An accepted file is kept by `capability:owner_sessions.keep_uploaded_file`, replacing the session's earlier one; a refused upload replaces nothing.
judgement.divergence: One implementation refuses a missing or malformed final delimiter, an impossible derived length, an extra part, or an inconsistent transport length and preserves the prior upload; another treats EOF or the first delimiter-like sequence as the file-part end and may accept and replace the prior upload, which the owner observes.
judgement.why: The framing step defines how to recognize and subtract a closing delimiter but states no outcome when that delimiter or the transport length is invalid, even though acceptance replaces session state.

witness.initial: A valid owner session may already hold an uploaded file, no migration closure exists, and the owner submits a bounded upload head with a valid CSRF part and a valid export in the file part but no valid final multipart delimiter.
outcomes: The malformed ending makes the upload unreadable or malformed; it is refused and the previously kept upload remains.
EOF is treated as the file-part end; the valid export is accepted and replaces the previously kept upload.
witness.observer: The owner sees either an upload refusal or the new import mapping and replacement of the kept upload.
basis: `module:owner_interface` serves the upload, the mapping and the confirmation pages. `module:upload_framing` reads an upload's multipart head — its first part the CSRF field, then the file part's headers — and frames the file part as a stream that ends where the part ends (owner, 2026-11-17).
An accepted file is kept by `capability:owner_sessions.keep_uploaded_file`, replacing the session's earlier one; a refused upload replaces nothing.

topics.topic: Source of the CSRF value when the session disappears before page rendering
questions: How does an admitted page request obtain its CSRF value if sign-out or the expiry pass ends and removes the session before the page is rendered?

quotes: The session's CSRF value, or none when no session of that identity exists or it has reached a limit.

`owner_interface` puts it only in the forms of the page it renders for that session and keeps nothing. The identity is looked up as the session check looks it up, compared in constant time; a session past a limit answers none, as it serves no request (A13 rule 2).
`_render_owner_page` receives the session's CSRF value, which `owner_sessions.give_session_csrf` gives for the cookie's session, or none — the sign-in page's form carries none (A13 rule 4).
judgement.why: The later public API and contract require a fresh lookup, return no CSRF value after the session disappears or expires, and render the no-value case as the sign-in page rather than caching the former value.
